title: Voiding a fiscal receipt after a merge refunds the payment but leaves the target order closed with a stale paid amount
description: mergeOrders moves the source's payments and items to the target (line 589), but fiscal_receipts.orderId stays on the source. If the source had a device-paid partial (receipt 'tamamlandi') and the fiscal receipt is later voided on the device (applySale status 99, simulator or webhook), refundExternalPayments(t, …, r.orderId = SOURCE, paymentIds) marks the payment (now on the target) as refunded. It then reopens and recalcs only the source, which is 'birlesti', so its status is not 'kapali'. The target keeps status 'kapali' and its stored paid still includes the refunded card payment. Result: a closed order with money still owed, the floor and list show it fully paid, and the X/Z report counts its full net sales but only the payments that remain.
fix: In refundExternalPayments, work from each payment's current orderId (p.orderId) rather than r.orderId: refund the payment, then reopen (if 'kapali') and recalc every order that owned a refunded payment. Alternatively, have mergeOrders move fiscal_receipts.orderId (and transferItems handle it too), or refuse to merge a source that has completed device receipts.

`S1 target after void { status: 'kapali', total: 47500, storedPaid: 47500, livePaid: 33500, refunded: [ 14000 ] }`

The bug is real. Confirmed with a runnable probe. The bug is real and it loses money and corrupts the Z without anyone being told.

**Root cause.** `mergeOrders` (server/services/orders.ts:588-589) moves the source order's items and payments to the target. It does not move `fiscal_receipts.orderId`, and it only blocks pending device receipts. So a completed (`tamamlandi`) receipt still points at the source. When the receipt is voided on the device (TokenX webhook or simulator, status 99), `applySale` (server/okc/service.ts:316) calls `refundExternalPayments(t, ..., r.orderId = SOURCE, r.paymentIds)`, which:
- marks the payment refunded, even though it now belongs to the target
- reopens and recalculates only the source, which is `birlesti`, so nothing reopens

The target keeps status `kapali` and its stored `paid` still includes the refunded payment.

**Probe:** /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/merge-void-impact.probe.test.ts. I also re-ran the original probe as /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/merge-okc-void.probe.test.ts, and it reproduced the same numbers: storedPaid 47500 vs live 33500, X netSales 47500 vs payments 33500.

**Control, same device void without a merge.** The order reopens correctly:
- `CONTROL (no merge) after void { status: 'acik', total: 14000, paid: 0 }`
- `CONTROL day close attempt 409`, so the open order blocks the Z until the money is collected again

**Scenario: partial device payment on A, merge A into B, B closes, receipt voided on the device:**
- `SCENARIO B after void { status: 'kapali', total: 47500, storedPaid: 47500, livePaid: 33500 }`
- `SCENARIO floor has open order on table B? false`
- The `okc.void` audit row points at the source order A (`birlesti`, total 0), not B, and its message says "ödeme geri alındı ve adisyon yeniden açıldı", but no order was reopened. This misleads staff.
- `SCENARIO day close status 200`: the open-order guard is bypassed.
- `Z summary { netSales: 61500, paymentsTotal: 47500, openOrdersAtClose: 0, expectedCash: 47500, cashDiff: 0 }`. Of the 140 TL gap, all comes from the voided card payment. The control order was settled, so it adds nothing.
- AssertionError: expected 61500 to be 47500.

**Real-world impact:**
1. The customer's 140 TL card charge is reversed on the device, but LafPOS shows the order closed and fully paid. No prompt asks staff to collect it again, so the money is lost silently.
2. The Z is stored and closed with net sales above recorded payments, and `summary.netSales` is what goes to lafmaliyet (days.ts:317). `cashDiff` stays 0, so nothing flags the gap.
3. The safety net that works without a merge (the order reopens and day close returns 409) is skipped.
4. The audit trail names the wrong order and says it was reopened.

**Trigger.** Every step is routine: one guest pays their part on the fiscal device, the tables are joined, the rest is paid, and the fiscal receipt is voided the same day, for example after a wrong card charge. The full sequence is uncommon, which is the only thing keeping this from critical. A manager who notices can reopen B by hand, since `reopenOrder` recalculates, but nothing in the system points them to B.

title: Voiding a device receipt after its order was merged refunds the target order's payments but leaves the target closed and 'paid'
description: `applySale` (status 99) calls `refundExternalPayments(t, ..., r.orderId, r.paymentIds)` with the receipt's original order. `mergeOrders` moves payments and items to the target order, but the receipt keeps the source orderId. The void therefore refunds payments that now belong to the target and decrements the target's item paidQty. It then recalculates and reopens only the source order, which is already merged. The target stays 'kapali' with a stale stored `paid`. The X/Z report counts the full closed-order total as net sales while the live payments are lower by the voided amount.
fix: In refundExternalPayments, work from each payment's current `orderId` rather than the receipt's. Recalculate and, if needed, reopen every order touched, and uncredit the customer on the order that is actually closed. Alternatively, have mergeOrders re-point fiscal_receipts.orderId to the target, or refuse to merge orders that have completed device receipts.

title: Fiscal receipt void reopens a closed order even when it refunds nothing (payment already refunded in LafPOS)
description: refundExternalPayments skips payments that are already refunded, but still reopens the order whenever it is 'kapali'. If a device card payment was refunded in LafPOS (refundPayment allows this for device payments) and the customer then paid cash, a later void of the original fiscal receipt reopens a fully paid order: status 'acik', due 0. The customer is also uncredited. The order then blocks gün sonu with open_orders until someone closes it by hand.
fix: Reopen (and uncredit) only if at least one payment was actually refunded in this call and the recalculated paid is below the total. Also consider refusing LafPOS-side refundPayment for payments linked to a completed fiscal receipt (require the device void instead), so the ÖKC and LafPOS Z stay in step.

   - P3: the cash payment closes the order; the customer shows visits 1, totalSpent 19500, stamps 1.
   - P4/P5: the device void returns 200. The order is then status 'acik', total 19500, paid 19500, due 0, and the only live payment is Nakit 19500. The customer is uncredited to visits 0, totalSpent 0, stamps 0.
   - P6: the okc.void alarm audit says "₺195,00 ödeme geri alındı ve adisyon yeniden açıldı", but nothing was refunded. The audit record is misleading.
   - P7: re-sending the order to the ÖKC is refused with 409 okc_partial, so reopening does not lead to a new fiscal receipt.
   - P8: gün sonu is blocked with 409 open_orders.

**Root cause.** In refundExternalPayments (server/services/orders.ts lines 1213-1240), already-refunded payments are skipped with `continue`. The order is still reopened and the customer uncredited whenever the status is 'kapali', whether or not anything was refunded or the paid amount fell below the total.

**Why low.** No money is miscounted, and staff can recover with one manual close. The real effects are a false alarm audit, a fully paid order shown as open, a temporary loss of customer credit, and a blocked gün sonu until someone closes the order by hand.

Confirmed with my own probe. The void reopens an order it refunded nothing on, and the order is then stuck.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-correctness/okc-void-after-refund-verify.probe.test.ts. Run with the given vitest config and the filter okc-void-after-refund-verify. The test fails with `expected 'acik' to be 'kapali'`.

Steps and output:
- Pay the order on the device (simulator) by card; the order has a customer attached. Result: `{ status: 'kapali', paid: 14000, visits: 1 }`.
- Refund that device card payment in LafPOS with Müdür PIN approval. Result: 200.
- Pay the same total in cash. Result: `cash closed: true { status: 'kapali', paid: 14000, live: ['Nakit'], visits: 1 }`.
- Void the receipt on the device (status 99). Result: `{ status: 'acik', total: 14000, paid: 14000, due: 0, live: ['Nakit'], visits: 0 }`. No payment was changed, but the order reopened and the customer's visit was taken back.
- The okc.void audit reads "₺140,00 ödeme geri alındı ve adisyon yeniden açıldı" with amount 14000. Nothing was refunded, so this message is false.
- Sending the order to the device again: `409 okc_partial`. Taking another payment: `409 nothing_due`. Gün sonu: `409 open_orders Açık adisyon var: #1`.
- Only the API `POST /orders/:id/close` fixes it (200, kapali, visits 1). The UI does not offer it: in src/pages/order/OrderPage.tsx:163, "Sıfır tutarlı adisyonu kapat" only shows when `order.total === 0`, and the Ödeme button is off when due <= 0. From the UI, staff can only refund the cash and take it again, or refund and cancel the order.

Why the current behaviour is not intended:
- docs/04-YAZARKASA.md §6 says status 99 refunds that receipt's payments and makes the order payable again.
- Here nothing was refunded and nothing is payable. So the reopen does not follow the documented intent.
- It also cannot get a new fiscal receipt issued, because sending to the device again is blocked with okc_partial.
- The `continue` in refundExternalPayments (server/services/orders.ts:1221) skips payments already refunded, but the `if (o.status === 'kapali')` reopen and uncreditCustomer at line 1233 run anyway.

The proposed fix is sound: reopen and uncredit only if this call actually refunded a payment and the recalculated paid is below the total. The audit message should also only say a payment was refunded when one was.

Why low severity:
- It needs an unusual order of steps: an approved LafPOS refund of a device payment, then paying again, then the device void.
- No money is wrong: paid, cash and the payment list stay correct, and the alarm is audited.
- The customer credit comes back on the manual close.
- The cost is an order that blocks gün sonu, cannot be closed from the UI, and leaves a misleading audit line.

The bug is real and its impact is small. No money is lost and the final Z is correct once the order is closed again. But the void puts a fully paid order back into an open state that staff cannot close from the UI, and it blocks gün sonu.

Probe: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/void-after-refund-impact.probe.test.ts

The probe uses a path the UI can reach. The order has Türk kahvesi and Latte M. Only the Türk kahvesi goes to the device, which takes card, so the order stays open with 195 TL due and the payment modal is available. The manager refunds the device payment in LafPOS, the cashier takes 335 TL cash, and the order closes. The fiscal receipt is then voided on the device. Output:
- after device void { status: 'acik', total: 33500, paid: 33500, due: 0, livePayments: [['Nakit', 33500]] }
- Z summary diff after the void: receipts 1→0, gross 33500→0, netSales 33500→0, kdv and topProducts emptied, openOrdersAtClose 0→1. While the order is reopened, the interim/X report shows no sales but the 335 TL cash is still counted.
- add payment → 409 nothing_due | cancel → 409 has_payments | gün sonu → 409 open_orders "Açık adisyon var: #1…"
- okc.void alarm audit says "₺140,00 ödeme geri alındı ve adisyon yeniden açıldı", but this call refunded nothing.
- POST /orders/:id/close through the API → 200 kapali, and the Z then matches the pre-void state exactly. So the damage reverses, but only through the API.

There is no direct UI way out. In OrderPage.tsx:
- The payment button is disabled when due <= 0.
- "Sıfır tutarlı adisyonu kapat" only shows when total === 0.
- "Adisyonu iptal et" only shows when paid === 0.
- "Yeniden aç" only shows when the order is kapali.

So on the floor, staff are stuck at gün sonu. They need someone to call the API, or a messy workaround with an approval and alarm audits (for example: add an item, refund the cash, void the item, pay again).

If a customer is attached to the order, they also lose credit until it is closed again.

Limits on reach:
- A fully paid device order cannot have its payment refunded from the UI (the payment modal needs due > 0). So the realistic path needs a partial, item-selected device basket, or a direct API call.
- The simulator refuses a void on a closed day, so the void-after-Z variant could not be reproduced (second probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-okanberkmanavoglu-Downloads/36639f88-6c66-4e9d-babe-a70914f282d6/scratchpad/audit/verify-state-r1-impact/void-after-refund-postz.probe.test.ts returned 409 day_closed).

That leaves a real but uncommon operational blocker plus a misleading audit and interim report, which fits low severity.

title: Service charge can never reach the device once every item has gone through per-item baskets
description: The service line is only added on a whole-order basket that still has unpaid items (`!input.selection && ... && parts.length`), and per-item baskets never carry service. The docs recommend paying item by item when each person needs their own receipt. In that flow every item ends up fiscalized and the service stays in the remaining balance. The next whole-order send then fails with 'Cihaza gönderilecek ücretli kalem yok', so the service has to be taken in LafPOS without a fiscal receipt. Result: the device total for the order is lower than the LafPOS total.
evidence:
order total 30800 service 2800
per-item basket 14000 ["Türk kahvesi"]
per-item basket 14000 ["Türk kahvesi"]
after per-item baskets: status acik total 30800 paid 28000 remaining 2800
send remaining (service) to device -> 400 {"error":"Cihaza gönderilecek ücretli kalem yok","code":"okc_basket"}
fix: When nothing chargeable is left but service (or service minus what was already fiscalized) is still due, build a basket that holds only the 'Servis ücreti' line. Alternatively, give per-item baskets their proportional service share. Either way, track how much service has already been sent to the device.

title: Second whole-order basket sends the full service again and hides the overlap as a fake discount, so the KDV split no longer matches LafPOS
description: After a whole-order basket that included a service line is paid, items can still be added (the docs allow this while the basket is pending). The next whole-order basket again sends `totals.service` in full, even though the first receipt already fiscalized part of it. The drift loop then pushes the overpaid service into an 'İndirim' adjust on whatever item is largest, regardless of its KDV rate. The order total still matches, but the device receipts show 71 TL of service where LafPOS has 43 TL. They also show a 28 TL discount that does not exist in LafPOS, and the gross per KDV rate differs between the two. If the new items are cheaper than the earlier service line, the send fails outright and the remainder cannot be fiscalized at all.
fix: Record how much service each receipt fiscalized (for example on fiscal_receipts) and send only `totals.service - alreadyFiscalizedService` as the service line. Book any drift only within the same KDV rate, and never as a discount on another rate's item.

title: Device sale whose payments don't cover the basket (ikram, ödemesiz or an unmapped type) still marks every item paid; the marks are orphaned and survive a receipt void
description: `salePayments` skips IKRAM (9) and ODEMESIZ (8) and clips to the basket, and `methodFor` can drop a payment. Despite that, `addExternalPayments` marks every line in `r.items` as paid. Only the first recorded payment carries those marks; when no payment survives, nothing carries them. The order stays open with an amount due, but its items are 'paid'. As a result the remainder cannot be resent to the device ('ücretli kalem yok'), and the items cannot be voided or comped (item_paid). The device receipt total (280 TL) differs from what LafPOS recorded (140 TL). With a full ikram, `r.paymentIds` is empty, so a later receipt void (99) takes the else branch and never clears paidQty.
fix: If the mapped payments sum to less than r.amount, do not mark items paid; mark the receipt 'hata' and raise an okc alarm. Ikram/ödemesiz on the device should become an audited comp or an alarm, never a silent skip. Keep the item marks with the receipt so a 99 void always reverts them, even when no payment row exists.

title: Receipt void (99) arriving by webhook after the day was closed refunds that day's payments and leaves an open order in the closed day
description: The simulator void path refuses payments that belong to a closed day ('Kapanmış bir güne ait fiş iptal edilemez'). The real TokenX webhook path (`handleTokenxWebhook` → `applySale` status 99) has no such check. It refunds payments whose dayId belongs to a closed business day and sets the order back to 'acik' inside that day. The stored Z (netSales/cash 28000) no longer matches the day's data (now 14000), and no later day close checks the orphaned open order. If the day is reopened or exported, it reports different numbers from the Z already taken.
evidence:
webhook 99 after day close -> 200
order after: status acik paid 0 payments [["Nakit",14000,true]]
closed day 2026-10-26 closedAt set true | stored Z: netSales 28000 cash 28000 | recomputed now: netSales 14000 cash 14000 openOrders 1
fix: Apply the same rule as simulatorCancel inside applySale for status 99: if any of r.paymentIds belongs to a day that is no longer open, do not refund. Instead write an 'okc.void_closed_day' alarm (or post the refund as a correction in the current day) and keep the receipt/order state consistent.

title: A fiscal-receipt void that arrives after day close rewrites the closed day, and the re-payment lands in the next Z with no sale behind it
description: applySale(status 99), reached from the TokenX webhook (handleTokenxWebhook, line 420), calls refundExternalPayments without checking the business day. The simulator path refuses this case ('Kapanmış bir güne ait fiş iptal edilemez', line 474), but the real device path does not. When a receipt from an already-closed day is voided on the device, three things happen. The closed day's payments get refundedAt. The order goes back to 'acik' inside the closed day. /reports/summary for that date drops, while the stored Z and the lafmaliyet payload still show the old figure. addPayment (server/services/orders.ts:825) then accepts payment on this orphan order on the next day: it uses requireOpenDay() for the payment's dayId and never checks o.dayId. The result is that the next Z gets payments (z_total) with zero net sales, and the old date shows net sales with no matching payments.
evidence:
Z1 at close: net 61500 z_total 615 cash 615
webhook 200 {"ok":true}
order A status acik dayId==day1 true
11-02 /reports/summary net 19500 payments [Nakit 19500] | stored Z net 61500 Z lafmaliyet z_total 615
repay status 200 true
Z2 net 0 Z2 z_total 420 Z2 card 420 receipts 0
11-02 report net now 61500 payments [["Nakit",19500]]
11-03 report net 0 payments [["Kredi kartı",42000]]
AssertionError: report for a closed date must still equal its Z: expected 19500 to be 61500
AssertionError: Z2 payments total equals Z2 net sales: expected 42000 to be +0
fix: In applySale's status-99 branch, apply the same rule as simulatorCancel. If any of r.paymentIds belongs to a day other than the open day (or no day is open), do not refund or reopen. Record an alarm audit entry ('fiş kapanmış güne ait; iade olarak işleyin') and mark the receipt as fis_iptal. In addPayment and addExternalPayments, also refuse orders whose dayId is not the open day (conflict 'day_closed').

title: A send error overwrites a receipt that was completed meanwhile with 'hata', so a later fiscal void no longer refunds
description: `sendOrderToDevice` inserts the receipt as 'gonderildi' and then awaits the TokenX POST. If the BASKET_COMPLETED webhook (or a poll) applies the sale while the POST is still in flight and the POST then fails (for example a gateway timeout), the catch block runs `update ... set status 'hata'` without checking the current status. The order is closed and paid, but the receipt reads 'hata' and the cashier gets a 502 'Yazarkasaya gönderilemedi'. When the receipt is later voided on the device (status 99), `r.status !== 'tamamlandi'` sends it down the else branch: the receipt becomes 'iptal' and the LafPOS payment is never refunded, even though the fiscal sale was cancelled.
evidence:
webhook during POST -> 200
send -> 502 {"error":"Yazarkasaya gönderilemedi: The operation was aborted due to timeout","code":"okc_send"}
receipt status hata error The operation was aborted due to timeout | order kapali paid 14000
after device void: receipt iptal | order kapali paid 14000
fix: Make the failure update conditional, e.g. `where id = ? and status in ('gonderildi','kilitli')`, and skip the 502 when the receipt is already 'tamamlandi'. Make the 99 handler key on `paymentIds.length` (non-refunded payments exist) rather than on status alone. Apply the same compare-and-set to cancelDeviceBasket's final update.

title: KDV split on the device diverges from LafPOS when an order discount is redistributed after a per-item device payment
description: `calcOrder` re-allocates the order-level discount over all lines on every recalc, including units already fiscalized on the device. When an item is added after a per-item device receipt, the already-printed item's LafPOS lineNet changes. The whole-order basket's drift loop then books the difference on the largest unpaid item, here a 20% KDV item, even though the shift came from a 10% item. Order totals match, but the device receipts and the LafPOS Z KDV table disagree per rate by 8.23 TL.
evidence: order kapali total 39000 | device receipts gross by KDV {"10":11586,"20":27414} | LafPOS (Z) gross by KDV {"10":12409,"20":26591}
fix: Freeze lineNet for units already paid or fiscalized (store each paid unit's net with its payment or receipt) and allocate the order discount only over unpaid units. Alternatively, restrict drift absorption to items of the KDV rate the drift came from, and refuse the send when that is not possible.

title: Basket that fails to send (timeout) is marked 'hata' and never reconciled: refresh and polling skip it, and LafPOS lets the order be charged again
description: Any TokenX send error, including an ambiguous network or gateway timeout after which the basket may still exist on the device, sets the receipt to 'hata'. `refreshReceipt` returns early for anything that is not 'gonderildi'/'kilitli', and the poll loop only selects those statuses. Without a webhook, LafPOS never asks Token whether that basket was paid. The order is unlocked, so the cashier can take the same amount again in LafPOS (or resend, which Token may reject with 1101). The device sale then exists with no LafPOS record, or is booked twice.
fix: Treat a timeout or network error (no Token status code) as 'belirsiz' (unknown): keep the order locked, poll GET /v1/basket for that receipt, and allow refresh for it. Only a definite Token error code should become 'hata'.

title: TokenX polling is not resumed after a server restart; baskets pending at boot are never queried
description: `ensurePolling()` is only called from `sendOrderToDevice`; nothing at startup restarts it. The kasa PC restarts the server, for example after saving ayarlar.env. Any TokenX basket still 'gonderildi' or 'kilitli' at that moment is never polled when no webhook is configured. The order stays locked with okc_pending until someone presses the manual refresh button or a new basket is sent.
evidence:
after 6 s: GET basket polls 0 | order status acik paid 0
LafPOS payment meanwhile -> 409 {"error":"Bu adisyonun sepeti yazarkasada bekliyor; önce cihazda ödeyin ya da sepeti iptal edin","code":"okc_pending"}
fix: At server start, call ensurePolling() when the provider is tokenx and any tokenx receipt is pending (for example from index.ts or jobs.ts).

title: Device cancel (-1) and basket cancel from LafPOS are not audited, although the docs say every result is
description: docs/04-YAZARKASA.md §6 says 'Her sonuç denetim kaydına yazılır'. The -1 branch of applySale writes no audit row, nor does the non-paid 99 branch. A normal `cancelDeviceBasket` (non-force) does not either. Only send, paid, void, force_cancel and late_paid are logged, so a basket sent and then withdrawn leaves no trace beyond okc.send.
fix: Add fx.audit entries for okc.cancelled (device -1, with source), okc.void on a non-completed receipt, and okc.delete in cancelDeviceBasket (with userId).
